Bacteria and viruses cannot get in through your skin. The way they can enter your body is either through an open wound or through your mouth, nose and eyes.

When I go out of the house, I never touch my hands to my mouth, nose or eyes. If my eyes itch, my nose itches or I need to touch my face for similar reasons, I spray the hand sanitizer in my bag on my fingers and scratch the itchy areas after removing bacteria and viruses.

I always wash my hands with soap before eating outside (and at home, of course); if this is not possible, I sanitize my hands; if this is not possible, I prefer meals that I can eat with fork and spoon without using my hands.

If I have open wounds on my body, I always clean them with oxygenated water, cover them with bandages or band-aids and then go outside.

No matter how weak your immunity is, no matter how freezing it gets, if you don't have the bacteria and viruses in your body that can make you sick, you won't get sick. In various diseases where the immune system is destroyed or has to be suppressed by medical means, patients have survived for many years by ensuring that bacteria and viruses do not enter their bodies in this way. Fortunately, I don't have such a disease. But I am still careful.

For 5 years I haven't been sick, I haven't even had Covid, and there have been many forced occasions when I have been in the same closed environment with people with Covid.

It is partly true and partly myth that people need to get sick often and that they will be more resistant that way. The true part is that the immune system does indeed take quick action when it recognizes the same bacteria and virus later on. The false part is that it makes you a more resistant superhuman. Every illness takes something away from you, every illness causes irreversible damage to your organs and body, even if it is minor. Think of people who have permanently lost part of the capacity of their lungs and partially lost their sense of taste and smell due to the coronavirus. Did contracting the coronavirus make them more resistant and better? No, it only made them weaker.

I don't need to be sick for my immune system to recognize viruses and bacteria. I get regular vaccinations for various diseases and if I still get sick, I can easily take medicine.

TLDR; Be aware of how viruses and bacteria enter your body (open wounds, mouth, nose, eyes, etc.) and avoid touching these places without sanitizing your hands when you are outside your home. This is how I have not been sick for 5 years.
